punchline: Jake Knapp did not ban his phone; he made every app something he had to reinstall.
thirty_sec: In 2012 Jake Knapp was playing with his sons when his older son asked what was on his phone. He deleted Twitter, Instagram, Facebook, YouTube, games, email and Safari, and kept music, podcasts, maps and the camera. It cost him his name as a fast email replier, but his attention span grew. If he needs an app, he reinstalls it and deletes it afterwards. Six years on, he still lived that way.
